notes: Turn 101 (his answers of 2026-10-23 14:05 UTC, experiments/t101-answers/JOEL-20261023-1405.md): 91.1 B: the main invitation first, then one borrowing for each job; this is old P6 without its first two sentences, with "For warmth," (the turn-100 test, experiments/t100-readers-edit/BORROW-ONE-COMPETENCY-TEST.md).

beside.label: Old P6, where it was (its first two sentences went to the new h3, and the first is cut)
beside.text: Most of us wouldn't open up to somebody who'd only just stopped being mean, or let them take care of us. That takes warmth, and if there isn't any yet, borrow some. Think of someone you remember fondly. How would they sit beside your little one? Just make sure it's someone who liked you the way you were.

### If the Love Isn't Coming Yet

rows.article: If the love still isn't coming, you can at least stop judging
notes: Turn 101 (his answers of 2026-10-23 14:05 UTC, experiments/t101-answers/JOEL-20261023-1405.md): 91.1 B: old P6's first sentence is cut as a near-repeat of this paragraph's last; its second ("That takes warmth, and if there isn't any yet, borrow some.") ends this paragraph now.

beside.label: Old P5
beside.text: If the love still isn't coming, you can at least stop judging your little one. Obviously no insults. Helpful advice is great, we all need advice. Let them absorb it at their pace. And don't expect a thank-you for the session, like they booked it. That's enough to start being the adult, even if it isn't enough yet for them to trust you.

notes: Turn 101 (his answers of 2026-10-23 14:05 UTC, experiments/t101-answers/JOEL-20261023-1405.md): 93.2, his two sentences added onto this paragraph, as he pasted them: "my bad, i was editing the version i had before that. we can add that onto the para about prosperity philosophy".

beside.text: And I’m certainly not preaching “prosperity philosophy,” even though it can seem to start at that. We still need to remember that if we can only be thankful for the good things we have, we can fall into the trap of thinking that what we have is happiness itself. I’m ultimately reaching for something much deeper.

notes: Turn 101 (his answers of 2026-10-23 14:05 UTC, experiments/t101-answers/JOEL-20261023-1405.md): 93.1, his words for this paragraph's first sentence: "right, change the next sentence in next para to: \"Of course, that’s not to say you should not try to suffer less, or get away from abusers\"" (the period added).

beside.label: Before
beside.text: Of course, that’s not to say you should not try to suffer less. The point of life, according to every spiritual tradition and religion, I think, is to suffer less, which first requires us to understand the cause of suffering, and what real suffering and real happiness are. If you, like Biggie Smalls, have come to understand that having money is not real happiness, that’s a big deal! That’s something to be grateful for. If we get a chance to meditate or pray today, while on the toilet, upon waking up, while ChatGPT is “thinking” for us, that’s something to be thankful for, for sure.
